clue.text: Signals left out of things like this

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for these things

parts.note: the clue points at itself: things like this are crossword clues

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the signals were omitted from items such as this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts given to performers or players are signals telling them when to act.

clue.text: Be upwardly mobile, since Conservative, on purpose

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Advice to climb the social ladder deliberately, given that one is a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise or climb is literally to move upwards, so it fits being upwardly mobile.

clue.text: Extremely short child in part of course, like some classes in biology

indicators.note: short means cut off its final letter

parts.note: extremely means very

indicators.note: the word for child sits inside the golf-course part

parts.note: a tee is the starting part of each hole on a golf course
a brat is an unruly child

explanation.surface: A very small child stands on part of a golf course, apparently like some biology classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims VERY to VER; the course is a golf course, where the TEE is the spot each hole starts from.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists group backboned animals such as mammals and birds as a taxonomic subphylum, so those classes are backboned ones.

clue.text: Main way to keep leaves from getting scattered

definitions.meaning: main as an adjective: chief, basic, as in a basic food

definitions.text: way to keep leaves from getting scattered
definitions.meaning: a wire fastener clips sheets of paper together

explanation.surface: The chief method of stopping autumn leaves blowing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food is the main one, and a staple is the wire clip that binds pages together.

clue.text: Disengage from seizure of power, with external order to get out

indicators.note: the proofreading order is placed outside, wrapping the seizure of power

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's instruction to delete, an order for text to get out
a coup is a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: Withdrawing from a coup when an outside power orders everyone to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: DELE is the printers' mark meaning 'delete', a convention the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple or separate two linked things is to disengage them.

clue.text: Members of colony, we hear, wind up in the Alps

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: bees are members of a hive colony

explanation.surface: Insects of a colony seem to be stirred up high in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like a phrasal verb, but it is the noun wind plus 'up in the Alps': a cold northerly wind of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The bise is a cold dry north wind blowing over Switzerland and the Alpine region.

clue.text: Shots from short distance fail in sporting competitions

indicators.note: the word for fail goes inside the competitions

parts.note: cups are trophy competitions in sport
to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: Shots from near range miss in sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographs or film shots taken near the subject are the camera term for near shots.

clue.text: Old hand mostly has an outstanding score

indicators.note: mostly means losing the final letter

parts.note: in bridge the four hands are North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: An elderly card-player holds most of an unpaid tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' is a bridge hand, named by compass point; WEST loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a debt still to settle is in debt, an outstanding score being an unpaid account.

clue.text: As dueller, perhaps, withdraw from sun's heat here

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone retreating from the sun's heat in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The dueller withdraws a sword from its scabbard; the definition is that sense of withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist draws a sword out of its scabbard before the fight.

clue.text: One of the relative gains acquired through union negotiations

definitions.text: One of the relative gains acquired through union negotiations

parts.words: One of the relative gains acquired through union negotiations
parts.note: reads like trade-union bargaining gains, but the union is a marriage, which brings new relatives

explanation.surface: A benefit won through trade union bargaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage brings a spouse's family as relatives gained by law, not blood.

clue.text: Son was visibly moved, did some housework

parts.note: someone who wept showed emotion visibly

explanation.surface: A son, plainly emotional, did some cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a broom on the floor is a routine domestic chore.

clue.text: Deals with crowds holding pacifist back

indicators.note: the crowds word contains the reversed pacifist

parts.note: presses as a verb means crowds or throngs

indicators.note: back means the letters for pacifist are read in reverse

parts.note: CO stands for conscientious objector, a pacifist

explanation.surface: Handles throngs that are carrying a pacifist back.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the usual crossword shorthand for a conscientious objector, someone who refuses military service on principle.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle or work through something, such as paperwork, is to deal with it.

clue.text: Everything we hear is ideal, but endlessly complicated

indicators.note: complicated signals that the letters are tangled into a new order
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: All we're told is perfect, but it's terribly complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BUT to BU; IDEAL and BU are then rearranged by 'complicated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever can be heard by the ear is by definition within hearing range.

clue.text: Forging equipment villain dismantled after disposing of duplicates

indicators.note: dismantled means taken apart and reassembled in another order
the repeated letters in the word villain each lose their second copy

explanation.surface: A villain wrecks the smithy's kit after getting rid of copies.
explanation.walkthrough: VILLAIN has two Ls and two Is; dropping the duplicates leaves VILAN, which 'dismantled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith hammers hot metal on this iron block, the core tool of a forge.

clue.text: Detachment of soldiers holding clubs in card game

indicators.note: the suit letter goes inside the card game

parts.note: piquet is a two-player card game
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Soldiers holding clubs in the middle of a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is a link here; this is a variant spelling of picket.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket, here in an old spelling, is a small body of troops posted on guard.

clue.text: Plant producing insane amount of beer

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy
a pint is the usual measure of beer served in a British pub

explanation.surface: A plant that makes a mad quantity of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies, a wild arum of British hedgerows, goes by this name.

clue.text: Guy taking drug after drinks

indicators.note: the drug letter is placed after the drinks

parts.note: teas are drinks
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man taking ecstasy after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or make fun of them, as is to rib or taunt.

clue.text: Role in Shakespearean comedy that's played by musician

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as a boy
a stringed instrument a little larger than the violin

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare part taken on by a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the Twelfth Night heroine and the alto instrument of the string family.

clue.text: Excel in running, having ways to escape stumble

parts.note: outs are ways out of a difficulty
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: To shine in a race, having ways to avoid falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun or outpace others is to beat them in running.

clue.text: What are the odds of Ulster creating employment?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word Ulster are taken

explanation.surface: A question about the chances of Northern Ireland generating jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is Northern Ireland; its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment of something means its application or the purpose it is put to.

clue.text: One's holding us up — that's inappropriate

indicators.note: the word for one contains the reversed us

parts.note: one, as in 'we are as one', means united; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is stopping us from moving, which isn't acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' as an adjective means joined together, as in 'the nation was one'; 'up' only works as a reversal because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-matched or unfit for a purpose is inappropriate to it.

clue.text: Rib other leading player with no end of humour

indicators.note: the picked final letter is dropped from the word for the other lead actor

parts.note: a co-star shares the lead role with another

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word humour

explanation.surface: Tease the other lead actor, lacking a sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' looks like the verb to tease, but it is the noun: the anatomical Latin term.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, the Latin term for a rib bone is used as its formal name.

clue.text: Parts of all answers, some 13 across in some answers singularly found in 14 and 22 across

definitions.text: Parts of all answers, some 13 across in some answers singularly found in 14 and 22 across

parts.words: Parts of all answers, some 13 across in some answers singularly found in 14 and 22 across
parts.note: every answer is made of these; ten short answers sound like the plural of one that appears once each in the entries at 14 and 22 across

explanation.surface: A themed description of what the short answers have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten answers sound like plural characters: CUES (Q), BISE (B), OWES (O), TEASE (T), WISE (Y), EYES (I), PEASE (P), SEIZE (C), USE (U), EASE (E); each occurs once in PICQUET or BIOTYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Words are built from alphabetic characters, so every grid answer is composed of them.

clue.text: Group of similar creatures silly boy and I pet

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish boy and I own a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use this term for organisms sharing the same genetic makeup.

clue.text: Capital got constricted?

annotationWithheld.why: 'Capital got constricted?' (6): GOT inside BOA, where 'constricted' must both supply BOA (constrictor) and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Birthday's ending soon, as it happens

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the birthday word

parts.note: early can mean soon, before long

explanation.surface: A birthday is ending soon, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' looks like 'by chance', but it means at the rate it occurs: once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual events recur every twelve months, which is how often a birthday comes round.

clue.text: Declining to have the electrical connexions put outside

indicators.note: the wiring word is placed around the word the

parts.note: wiring is the set of electrical connections in a building

explanation.surface: Reluctance to have the electric cables installed outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link; 'connexions' is an old spelling of connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that are wilting or fading are in decline, shrivelling away.

clue.text: Royal I spotted around is showing good judgment

indicators.note: the royal pronoun is placed around the word is

parts.note: the royal we is the monarch's way of saying I

explanation.surface: A royal personage, seen nearby, displays sound judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' is a link; the 'royal we' is how a monarch traditionally refers to themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sage or prudent shows sound judgment.

clue.text: Keeps watch on stern of frigate? That's right

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the last letter of frigate is taken

parts.note: yes is said to confirm something is right

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a lookout from the back of a warship and is told it's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' is nautical, fitting the frigate, but it just means the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, watching it.

clue.text: Pressure moderate in old person's pulse

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to ease is to lessen or moderate

explanation.surface: Blood pressure moderating in an elderly patient's pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks medical, but it means edible seeds such as lentils; 'old' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are legume seeds, and this archaic word meant peas, as in the nursery rhyme 'pudding hot'.

clue.text: No difficulty completing puzzle, kinda obvious and simple

indicators.note: the letters completing each of these words, their last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: The puzzle was finished without trouble, being sort of plain and straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link, giving no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with effortless facility means doing it without any trouble.

clue.text: Measure covering energy capture

indicators.note: the measure word wraps around the energy letter

parts.note: size is a measure of how big something is
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gauge enclosing energy so as to trap it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab or take hold of something forcibly is to capture it.

clue.text: Snares fish in cod nets

indicators.note: the fishing word goes inside the rearranged nets
cod means fake or bogus, so the word nets is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A trap for fish made from nets for cod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' looks like the fish, fitting the nets, but is the adjective meaning sham or mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare or trap something is to catch it in tangles.
